symptom: in a run of create entity / create association statements, judging each held write was 35% of the stage (ako/mxcli#2160): Writer.judgeHeld 2.9 s of 8.2 s sampled for 300 entities and 299 associations, 1.7 s of it in canon.Equal
cause: judgeHeld compared the new write with the write the run already held through canon.Equal, which digests both documents: the held domain model was unmarshalled, numbered and hashed again for every statement, although it had been the 'new' side of the statement before
file: modelsdk/mpr/writer_deferred.go (deferredWrite.judgedDigest, judgeHeld, judgedDigest), modelsdk/mpr/writer_core.go (JudgedDigests counter), mdl/backend/modelsdk/backend.go
insight: The digest that is free to keep is the one of the identity-carried form, not of the normalised form the run used to hold, so the run now holds the carried form. That changes no verdict - the next write takes the same top-level identity fields before it is compared, so both sides hold them either way - and the existing reporting test (a settled re-run reports nothing, one changed statement reports alone) is what says so. Two shortcuts were measured and dropped before writing anything: an unchanged statement's write is byte-identical to the held one in only 29 of 569 cases, because a re-declared entity gets fresh element $IDs that the digest numbers away and bytes do not; and comparing un-normalised digests cannot work for the reason normalisation was added (a rebuilt entity lacks what the writer completes). Count test: 2.0 digests per added statement before, 1.0 after. The seed: 7.1 s -> 6.4 s first run, 9.6 s -> 8.7 s settled re-run, output identical on four runs including one with a single changed statement. What is left in judgeHeld is normalizeForStorage, five passes that each unmarshal the document.
